title: As Paramount Settlement Talks With States Progress, Some AGs Are Pushing for Stronger Restrictions
content:
On Sunday, settlementtalks between Paramount and the state attorneys general that suedto block itsWarner Bros. Discoverydeal continued — but there was no resolution by the end of the day.

But while California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading the 12-state coalition’s antitrust litigation, is said to be open to considering a set of conditions that would put certain restrictions on Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros., at least two other AGs are pushing for stricter measures before they sign off on anything.

Over the weekend, the sideshashed out potential terms of a settlement. The sides were expected to put the negotiations on hiatus on Monday for the Yom Kippur holiday.

The terms discussed were said to include Paramount agreeing to operate Warner Bros.’ studio operations separately for a time (something Paramount chief David Ellison already said he was willing to do). Also on the table was a requirement that the mergedParamount-Warner Bros.release at least 30 films theatrically per year (a promise Ellisonhas already made, repeatedly), with financial penalties if they fail to hit that mark. In addition, the two sides also discussed a binding guarantee from Paramount that it would not relocate its existing California operations (as Ellison has threatened to do) and the formation of a third-party “editorial adviser” to oversee CNN and CBS News.

But some of the states want more.

New York Attorney General Letitia James, for one, wants Paramount to commit to specific job-protection guarantees, including for employees at Warner Bros., sources confirmed. Paramount has claimed it would achieve $6 billion in cost savings by merging with WBD — and that would imply thousands of layoffs.

In addition, Connecticut Attorney General William Tong is opposed to the current proposed settlement terms with Paramount,Varietyconfirmed. A source familiar with the AG’s position said he wants any agreement to include stronger provisions guaranteeing that CNN and CBS News remain independent from interference from Paramount’s owners, with more teeth than a third-party “adviser.” Details of the pushback by the New York and Connecticut AGs has been previously reported byCNNand the media industry newsletterStatus.

The battle has taken on political overtones given the connections ofParamount SkydanceCEO David Ellison and his family to President Donald Trump. The Justice Department and FCC have approved the transaction without asking for any concessions or remedies — an unusually hands-off approach for such a large horizontal merger. That opened the door for the 12 states to flex their legal muscle to scrutinize the combination.

David Ellison has voiced his belief, which is shared by other critics of the AGs’ legal maneuver, that the opposition to Paramount-WBD is about his control CNN — rather than antitrust concerns. “I believe this fight is not really about market share,” Ellison wrote ina New York Times op-ed. “I believe a plainer worry sits beneath the briefs and the news releases: the news. The issue is whether I can be trusted as a steward of Warner’s CNN.” Ellison has pledged that CNN and CBS News journalists “will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause.”

The lawsuit filed by the 12 states and a similar antitrust case filed by the Writers Guild of America West are the last obstacles holding up Paramount’s closing of the WBD acquisition. It’s been a wild, yearlong chase that included Paramount having to outbid Netflix, which reached a deal to buy Warner Bros. and HBO n early December. The streaming giant was out of the picture by late February.

Even if Paramount is able to reach a settlement with the state AGs, the Paramount-WB merger will not close immediately, a knowledgeable source toldVariety. Because of the $110 billion pact’s intricate financing — including some$24 billion from Middle Eastern government funds— and other factors, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will need at least a week or so after any deal with the states is in place.

Tong, after the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California granted the states’ request for a temporary restraining order halting the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger in July, said in an official statement: “This is a critical victory for American consumers, for objective and independent journalism, and for the workers, actors, artists and fans of our country’s celebrated film and television industry. We are suing to protect free and fair competition, choice and quality programming. This order demonstrates the strength of our case and the power of states stepping in to fill the void left by Trump’s absent Department of Justice.”

And New York’s James, after the 12 states initially filed their lawsuit in July, said in a statement: “For over a century, Paramount and Warner Bros. have competed to create movies and television that bring people together, inspire and sustain generations of artists, and help us understand the world. This merger would destroy that competition, creating a massive company with unprecedented power and influence over news and entertainment across the globe. Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. threatens to raise costs for consumers and put jobs and businesses nationwide at risk.”
title_zh: 隨著派拉蒙(Paramount)與各州的和解談判進展，一些州檢察總長(AGs)正在推動更嚴格的限制措施。
content_zh:
在星期日，派拉蒙(Paramount)與起訴阻止其華納兄弟(Warner Bros.)交易的州檢察總長之間的和解談判持續進行——但到一天結束時仍未達成任何解決方案。

據說，加州檢察總長羅伯·邦塔(Rob Bonta)，他是這個由12個州組成的反壟斷訴訟聯盟的領導者，對考慮一系列條件持開放態度，這些條件將對派拉蒙收購華納兄弟施加某些限制，但至少還有兩位其他檢察總長在他們簽署任何協議之前，要求更嚴格的措施。

在週末，雙方討論了潛在的和解條款。預計雙方將在星期一因為贖罪日(Yom Kippur)假期暫停談判。

據說討論的條款包括派拉蒙同意在一段時間內單獨運營華納兄弟的工作室業務（派拉蒙首席執行官大衛·艾利森(David Ellison)已表示他願意這樣做）。此外，合併後的派拉蒙-華納兄弟每年至少在影院上映30部電影的要求也在討論之中（艾利森已經多次做出這個承諾），如果未能達到這一標準，將面臨財務懲罰。此外，雙方還討論了派拉蒙提供一項具有約束力的保證，承諾不會將其現有的加州業務搬遷（正如艾利森所威脅的那樣），以及成立一個第三方“編輯顧問”來監督CNN和CBS新聞。

但一些州希望更多。

紐約檢察總長萊蒂西亞·詹姆斯(Letitia James)希望派拉蒙承諾具體的工作保護保證，包括對華納兄弟員工的保護，消息來源確認。派拉蒙聲稱通過與華納兄弟合併將實現60億美元的成本節省——這意味著數千人將被裁員。

此外，康涅狄格州檢察總長威廉·唐(William Tong)反對目前與派拉蒙的和解條款，《綜藝雜誌》(Variety)確認。一位熟悉檢察總長立場的消息來源表示，他希望任何協議都能包括更強有力的條款，保證CNN和CBS新聞不受派拉蒙所有者的干擾，這比第三方“顧問”更具約束力。紐約和康涅狄格州檢察總長的反對細節之前已被CNN和媒體行業通訊《Status》報導。

由於派拉蒙Skydance首席執行官大衛·艾利森及其家族與總統唐納德·特朗普(Donald Trump)的關係，這場戰鬥已帶上政治色彩。司法部和聯邦通信委員會(FCC)已批准該交易，並未要求任何讓步或補救措施——這對於如此大型的橫向合併而言是一種異常的放手方式。這為12個州提供了法律力量，以審查這一合併。

大衛·艾利森(David Ellison)表達了他的看法，這一觀點也受到其他對於州檢察長(AGs)法律手段的批評者的認同，他認為對於派拉蒙-華納兄弟探索(Paramount-WBD)的反對，實際上是關於他對CNN的控制，而非反壟斷問題。“我相信這場鬥爭其實並不是關於市場份額，”艾利森在《紐約時報》(New York Times)的專欄中寫道。“我相信在法律文件和新聞稿之下，還有一個更明顯的擔憂：新聞。問題在於我是否能被信任作為華納的CNN的管理者。”艾利森承諾，CNN和CBS新聞的記者“將繼續對事實和所有他們服務的人負責，而不是對任何政黨或事業負責。”

由12個州提起的訴訟以及美國西部編劇工會(Writers Guild of America West)提起的類似反壟斷案件，是阻礙派拉蒙完成華納兄弟探索收購的最後障礙。這是一場持續一年的激烈追逐，派拉蒙不得不超越Netflix的出價，Netflix在12月初達成了收購華納兄弟和HBO的協議。到了2月底，這家串流巨頭已經退出了競爭。

即使派拉蒙能夠與州檢察長達成和解，派拉蒙與華納兄弟的合併也不會立即完成，一位知情人士告訴《綜藝》(Variety)。由於這項1100億美元協議的複雜融資——包括來自中東政府基金的約240億美元——以及其他因素，派拉蒙和華納兄弟探索在與各州達成任何協議後，至少需要一週左右的時間。

在美國加州北區地區法院於七月批准各州要求的臨時禁令，暫停派拉蒙與華納兄弟探索的合併後，唐(Tong)在官方聲明中表示：“這對美國消費者、客觀和獨立的新聞業，以及我們國家備受讚譽的電影和電視產業的工人、演員、藝術家和粉絲來說是一個關鍵的勝利。我們提起訴訟是為了保護自由和公平的競爭、選擇和高品質的節目。這項命令顯示了我們案件的強大和各州介入填補特朗普缺席的司法部留下的空白的力量。”

而紐約的詹姆斯(James)在12個州最初於七月提起訴訟後表示：“在過去的百年裡，派拉蒙和華納兄弟一直在競爭，創造出能夠團結人們、啟發和支持幾代藝術家的電影和電視，並幫助我們理解世界。這項合併將摧毀這種競爭，創造出一個擁有前所未有的權力和影響力的龐大公司，影響全球的新聞和娛樂。派拉蒙收購華納兄弟的計劃威脅到消費者的成本，並使全國的工作和企業面臨風險。”
